title: Engineering mathematics
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for engineering mathematics, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Model selection and units
notes.body: Translate the stated geometry or physical relation into variables first, keep units consistent, and test whether the requested result is a value, rate, vector magnitude, or dimensionless quantity.

notes.heading: Calculus and optimization
notes.body: Derivatives give instantaneous rates and locate candidate extrema; definite integrals accumulate a rate over an interval. Verify endpoints and physical constraints before accepting an optimum.

notes.heading: Linear algebra and system behavior
notes.body: A determinant tests singularity for a square system, while eigenvectors identify directions whose orientation is preserved by a linear transformation. Pole location and residual patterns diagnose dynamic stability and model inadequacy.

notes.heading: Data and uncertainty
notes.body: Use averages only for the intended population, interpret confidence-interval width as uncertainty rather than error, and treat convergence or residual patterns as evidence about a method rather than proof of the underlying model.

title: Engineering sciences
summary: Focused, source-traceable review for dimensional reasoning and foundational physical-science relationships used in the linked Mechanical Engineering items; chemistry, specialist electrical design, and unrelated science breadth are excluded.

notes.heading: Dimensional reasoning
notes.body: Mechanical power has dimensions of energy per time, so force times velocity and torque times angular speed are consistent forms. Dimensional agreement is necessary but does not by itself validate a model.

notes.heading: Electrical response
notes.body: For series AC resistance and inductive reactance, combine perpendicular impedance components by magnitude; distinguish impedance from resistance and keep phase behavior separate from scalar addition.

notes.heading: Measurement response
notes.body: Calibration points support linearity only over the observed range. Examine slope, scatter, uncertainty, and residual pattern before extrapolating or claiming exact behavior.

notes.heading: Engineering evidence
notes.body: When an input property has wide measured spread, propagate or bound that uncertainty and obtain representative data when the decision is sensitive; do not hide variability behind a single nominal value.

notes.heading: Periodic quantities
notes.body: For a stated periodic process, frequency is cycles per unit time and period is its reciprocal. Use the stated interval and units; this is a basic physical-quantity interpretation, not machine-dynamics design.

notes.heading: AC impedance boundary
notes.body: For a supplied ideal series resistance and inductive reactance, treat the orthogonal components as a complex impedance: magnitude is the vector magnitude and phase is the arctangent of reactance over resistance. Exclude circuit design, component selection, and specialist electrical-engineering code requirements.

title: Statics and dynamics
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for statics and dynamics, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Free-body discipline
notes.body: Isolate the body, show every external force and couple, choose axes, and only then write equilibrium or motion equations. A missing action cannot be repaired by later algebra.

notes.heading: Work, impulse, and momentum
notes.body: Net work changes kinetic energy; external impulse changes momentum. Conservation statements apply only after defining a system and checking the corresponding external transfer.

notes.heading: Rotation and mechanisms
notes.body: Torque is force times perpendicular moment arm. Angular acceleration follows change in angular velocity over time, while natural frequency reflects the ratio of stiffness to inertia.

notes.heading: Two-dimensional motion
notes.body: Resolve projectile velocity into orthogonal components, use the same elapsed time for each direction, and apply level-ground range relations only when their stated assumptions hold.

title: Mechanics of materials
summary: Source-backed mechanics-of-materials review for stress, strain, deformation, stability, and failure-mode interpretation.

notes.heading: Model and units
notes.body: Define the load path, section geometry, sign convention, and compatible units before calculating. Use N and mm for MPa when convenient, or N and m consistently; do not mix diameter and radius formulas.

notes.heading: Stress and deformation
notes.body: Average axial stress is P/A, normal strain is change in length divided by original length, and elastic elongation is PL/(AE) when the member is prismatic and within the elastic range. Free thermal strain is alpha times the temperature change; full restraint converts it into stress E alpha delta-T.

notes.heading: Bending, torsion, and combined loading
notes.body: Use bending stress M/Z and torsional stress Tr/J with the stated section property. At a critical point, retain signs when superposing axial and bending stress; for combined stress use the supplied principal, Tresca, or von Mises criterion rather than comparing one component alone.

notes.heading: Stability and failure
notes.body: Euler buckling is an ideal elastic-column model and depends on effective length squared. Fatigue calculations require mean and alternating stress plus the stated endurance model; a calculated factor of safety is conditional on those assumptions, not a guarantee of life.

notes.heading: Common checks
notes.body: Check whether expansion is free or restrained, whether a column is slender enough for Euler theory, whether the critical fiber is tensile or compressive, and whether the answer has stress, strain, force, moment, or energy units.

title: Fluid mechanics
summary: Source-backed fluid-mechanics review for conservation, pressure, internal flow, momentum, losses, and pump behavior.

notes.heading: Control volume and properties
notes.body: State the control volume, density assumption, inlet and outlet directions, and whether pressure is gauge or absolute. For a filled incompressible section, Q equals mean velocity times area; use mass flow rho-Q for momentum.

notes.heading: Pressure and energy
notes.body: Hydrostatic gauge pressure is rho-g-h. Bernoulli or the steady-flow energy equation requires consistent datum, pressure convention, velocity terms, pump/turbine work, and loss terms; do not use gauge pressure as an absolute thermodynamic state.

notes.heading: Flow regime and losses
notes.body: Reynolds number selects the flow-regime interpretation. Darcy-Weisbach loss is f(L/D)V-squared/(2g), while minor losses use K V-squared/(2g); friction-factor convention and pipe diameter must be stated.

notes.heading: Momentum and machines
notes.body: A turning jet or elbow produces force from the vector change in momentum, not from speed change alone. Pump hydraulic power is rho-g-Q-H and shaft power is hydraulic power divided by efficiency. Affinity laws apply only within their stated similarity assumptions.

notes.heading: Engineering checks
notes.body: Check continuity, sign direction, units, cavitation margin, and whether a pump curve and system curve are being compared at the same flow. A plausible number with the wrong control-volume boundary is still wrong.

notes.heading: Hydroelectric conversion path
notes.body: For a hydroelectric system, available water energy depends on flow and elevation change (head); the penstock carries water to a turbine, and the turbine drives a generator. Keep hydraulic input, turbine shaft output, and electrical output at their stated boundaries, applying supplied efficiencies and losses only once. The DOE overview supports this general chain; PRC materials continue to define local examination scope.

title: Thermal science
summary: Source-backed thermal-science review for closed systems, control volumes, properties, entropy, heat transfer, and HVAC performance.

notes.heading: Energy accounting
notes.body: For a closed system use delta-U = Q - W when heat into the system and work done by the system are positive. For steady devices use the control-volume balance and explicitly state neglected kinetic, potential, heat, or work terms.

notes.heading: Properties and state
notes.body: Use absolute temperature in gas and radiation relations, distinguish specific from total quantities, and apply ideal-gas relations only when the idealization is stated or defensible. A throttling result of approximately constant enthalpy depends on steady, adiabatic, negligible-work assumptions.

notes.heading: Heat transfer
notes.body: Conduction, convection, radiation, and thermal-resistance networks use different governing relationships. Heat-exchanger calculations need a consistent terminal-temperature arrangement and an appropriate mean temperature difference; Celsius may be used for differences but not as an absolute radiation temperature.

notes.heading: Cycles and moist air
notes.body: Thermal efficiency is net work divided by heat input; refrigerator COP is cooling effect divided by work input and can exceed one. Separate sensible and latent loads when selecting a humidity-control response.

notes.heading: Irreversibility checks
notes.body: Friction generates entropy, intercooling can reduce multistage compression work, and a cold stream in an ordinary passive exchanger cannot exceed the hot-stream inlet temperature. Use these limits to test a numerical result.

title: Heat transfer
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for heat transfer, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Resistance networks
notes.body: For one-dimensional steady heat flow, series thermal resistances add and heat rate equals the driving temperature difference divided by total resistance.

notes.heading: Convection and extended surfaces
notes.body: Convection rate is hA times the surface-to-fluid temperature difference. Fins help when the extra effective area more than offsets their temperature decline and contact limitations.

notes.heading: Radiation
notes.body: Ideal blackbody emissive power is proportional to absolute temperature to the fourth power; Celsius values cannot be substituted into that relation.

notes.heading: Heat exchangers
notes.body: A cold stream can approach but not exceed the hot inlet temperature in an ordinary passive exchanger. Use Q=UA times the log-mean temperature difference when U, area, flow arrangement, and terminal temperatures support that model.

title: Power systems
summary: Source-backed power-cycle review for turbines, boilers, engines, combustion, heat exchange, and plant performance.

notes.heading: Cycle boundary
notes.body: Define heat input, heat rejection, net work, and device work before calculating efficiency or power. For an adiabatic turbine with negligible kinetic and potential changes, specific work follows the enthalpy drop.

notes.heading: Steam and gas-cycle reasoning
notes.body: Keep the idealized Otto, Diesel, Brayton, and Rankine heat-addition or component assumptions distinct. Reheat, regeneration, economizers, condensers, and intercooling change performance for identifiable thermodynamic reasons.

notes.heading: Boiler and engine performance
notes.body: Boiler efficiency compares useful fluid energy gain with fuel input; mechanical efficiency compares brake output with indicated or internal power. Specific fuel consumption uses mass fuel per unit brake output and requires a time conversion.

notes.heading: Combustion accounting
notes.body: Balance the fuel-oxidizer reaction before applying air-fuel or excess-air reasoning. Excess air can reduce peak temperature and change exhaust composition, but it does not create energy.

notes.heading: Plant checks
notes.body: Separate shaft output, fluid power, heat input, and auxiliary consumption. A complete-cycle energy balance must close, and any claimed efficiency must remain below the stated ideal or physical limit.

title: Refrigeration and HVAC
summary: Source-backed fundamentals for refrigeration-cycle performance, psychrometric interpretation, sensible/latent loads, and basic HVAC operation, with an explicit boundary against current-code and refrigerant-specific claims.

notes.heading: Pumps and systems
notes.body: Compare pump head and system head at the same flow. Series pumps add head at common flow; parallel pumps add flow at common head. Hydraulic power is rho-g-Q-H and shaft power includes efficiency.

notes.heading: Compressors
notes.body: Compressor efficiency compares ideal isentropic work with actual work for the same end states. Volumetric efficiency relates actual intake volume to displacement; clearance, valve losses, leakage, and temperature affect the result.

notes.heading: Refrigeration and HVAC
notes.body: Refrigerator COP is Q-cold/W, heat-pump COP is Q-hot/W, and Q-hot equals Q-cold plus work for the ideal energy balance. Separate sensible and latent loads and address moisture when humidity is the problem.

notes.heading: Heat exchangers and air
notes.body: Use UA-delta-Tlm or an energy balance only when terminal temperatures and flow arrangement support it. Duct velocity follows Q/A, fan power is Q-delta-p/efficiency, and fouling raises resistance and lowers heat transfer.

notes.heading: Operating checks
notes.body: Cavitation symptoms require an available-versus-required suction-head check. Superheat protects a compressor from liquid, while condenser heat rejection is cooling effect plus compressor work.

notes.heading: Stable HVAC principles and currentness boundary
notes.body: Refrigeration energy balances, COP relationships, sensible/latent load distinction, and psychrometric interpretation are treated as stable technical principles when state points and assumptions are supplied. Refrigerant restrictions, safety classifications, energy-code requirements, and edition-specific equipment standards are version-sensitive and excluded unless a current controlling source is attached. Technical support does not by itself establish MELE exam scope.

title: Machine design
summary: Source-backed machine-design review for shafts, gears, belts, chains, bearings, clutches, fatigue, and design limits.

notes.heading: Power path
notes.body: Trace torque, speed, force, power, and efficiency across each interface. Rotating power is T-omega, with rpm converted to radians per second; a gear ratio changes speed and torque in opposite directions in the ideal model.

notes.heading: Capacity equations
notes.body: Use the supplied shaft torsion, belt traction, clutch, bearing-life, spring, or brake model with compatible dimensions. Distinguish kinematic ratios from strength, wear, thermal, and fatigue capacity.

notes.heading: Fatigue and mean stress
notes.body: Separate alternating and mean stress and apply the stated Goodman or Soderberg relation. A safety factor from a simplified model must be interpreted with the load history, surface, notch, temperature, and material assumptions visible.

notes.heading: Bearings and lubrication
notes.body: Bearing rating is not a complete diagnosis. Equivalent load, duty, lubrication viscosity, contamination, alignment, heat generation, and speed all affect service behavior. Correct the mechanism before treating a rating as the answer.

notes.heading: Design judgment
notes.body: Choose the component or material that satisfies the stated load, environment, life, manufacturability, and maintenance constraints. Do not select by one attractive property while ignoring the governing failure mode.

title: Machine elements
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for machine elements, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Gear kinematics and force
notes.body: For an external gear pair, speed varies inversely with tooth count. Tangential pitch-line force equals transmitted torque divided by pitch radius, with torque and radius in consistent units.

notes.heading: Belts and chains
notes.body: Belt traction depends on friction and wrap together with usable tension. Chain speed follows sprocket teeth times pitch times revolutions per unit time, converted to the requested linear unit.

notes.heading: Bearings and lubrication
notes.body: Bearing selection considers equivalent load and accumulated duty, while overheating also requires checking lubricant viscosity, supply, contamination, alignment, and generated heat.

notes.heading: Power-transmission checks
notes.body: Trace torque, speed, force, and power through the component interfaces; distinguish kinematic ratios from capacity limits and efficiency losses.

title: Manufacturing processes
summary: Source-backed manufacturing review for machining, CNC setup, tolerances, process capability, production flow, and quality decisions.

notes.heading: Machining variables
notes.body: Turning speed is pi-D-N, feed rate is feed per revolution times rotational speed, material-removal rate depends on the stated process geometry, and ideal cutting power is force times cutting speed. Convert rpm, mm, and m consistently.

notes.heading: Datums and tolerances
notes.body: A workpiece datum connects the programmed coordinate system to the physical part. Worst-case stack-up adds absolute tolerances; fit decisions compare the limiting hole and shaft dimensions rather than nominal values alone.

notes.heading: Process capability
notes.body: Cp describes potential spread against specification width, while Cpk also reflects centering. Control limits describe process behavior and are not the same as specification limits; a signal prompts investigation rather than proving a cause.

notes.heading: Flow and economics
notes.body: Takt time is available production time divided by demand, the slowest required station limits sustainable throughput, and EOQ or break-even calculations are conditional on their cost assumptions. Kanban responds to downstream consumption and limits work in process.

notes.heading: Selection checks
notes.body: Match tool, material, geometry, tolerance, finish, machine limits, production volume, and measurement capability. A formula result does not override fixturing, tool wear, coolant, or safety constraints.

title: Industrial engineering
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for industrial engineering, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Flow and bottlenecks
notes.body: System throughput cannot sustainably exceed its slowest required station. Identify the longest cycle time, then compare it with takt or required cycle time derived from available production time and demand.

notes.heading: Inventory decisions
notes.body: EOQ balances annual ordering and holding costs under its simplifying assumptions; use the supplied demand, order cost, and unit holding cost without treating the result as universally optimal.

notes.heading: Pull production
notes.body: A kanban authorizes replenishment or movement based on downstream consumption, limiting work in process rather than serving as a forecast-only production order.

notes.heading: Capacity and improvement
notes.body: Measure acceptable output over actual operating time, locate the binding constraint, and improve or rebalance it before optimizing non-bottleneck stations.

title: Maintenance and quality
summary: Source-backed maintenance and reliability review for failure models, condition monitoring, quality signals, and safe energy control.

notes.heading: Reliability models
notes.body: For a constant failure rate, R(t)=exp(-lambda-t) and MTBF=1/lambda. Series reliability multiplies independent reliabilities, while parallel redundancy is one minus the product of failure probabilities. Use the model only within its assumptions.

notes.heading: Availability and improvement
notes.body: Steady-state availability is MTBF/(MTBF+MTTR). OEE multiplies availability, performance, and quality. An indicator diagnoses where to investigate; it does not by itself identify root cause.

notes.heading: Condition and quality evidence
notes.body: A rising vibration or temperature trend justifies an inspection plan before a threshold is crossed. Control-chart signals call for special-cause investigation, while capability indices describe spread and centering against specifications.

notes.heading: Failure analysis
notes.body: FMEA risk-priority numbers combine the supplied severity, occurrence, and detection ratings. Use the failure mode and effects to prioritize action; do not treat a score as a physical law.

notes.heading: Safe intervention
notes.body: Before removing a guard or opening equipment, isolate hazardous energy, release or block stored energy, and verify the safe state under the applicable procedure. Production urgency does not substitute for energy control.

title: Engineering economics
summary: Concept-focused Mechanical Engineering review for engineering economics, with governing relationships, assumptions, and interpretation checks used by linked practice items.

notes.heading: Cash-flow comparison
notes.body: Compare alternatives on a common time basis and include relevant acquisition, operating, energy, maintenance, and residual cash flows rather than choosing by first cost alone.

notes.heading: Present worth
notes.body: Discount future cash flows to the selected comparison date. For a uniform end-of-period series, multiply the recurring amount by the supplied present-worth factor when its rate and number of periods match.

notes.heading: Economic assumptions
notes.body: State the analysis period, interest rate, timing convention, and included costs. A numerical result is conditional on those assumptions rather than an intrinsic property of the machine.

notes.heading: Decision interpretation
notes.body: Prefer the economically favorable feasible alternative after technical, safety, and service requirements are met; a lower modeled cost does not excuse a design that fails those requirements.

title: REE Mathematics and Quantitative Methods
summary: Algebra, complex quantities, calculus, probability, and engineering economics.

notes.heading: Use in practice
notes.body: Apply the relationships and decision checks to connect calculation results to safe electrical-engineering decisions.

notes.heading: Linear systems: eliminate and check
notes.body: Align like variables. Add equations when a variable has opposite coefficients; otherwise multiply an equation by a nonzero factor first. Solve, substitute into an original equation, and verify both. For 2x + y = 11 and x − y = 1, addition gives 3x = 12, so x = 4 A; substitution gives y = 3 A.

title: REE Circuit Analysis Foundations
summary: Source-first REE review of DC network analysis, equivalent circuits, conservation laws, transient storage, and diagnostic reasoning.

notes.heading: Model and conservation
notes.body: Use an explicit lumped-circuit model. Apply Kirchhoff current law at nodes and Kirchhoff voltage law around loops; state reference directions and signs before solving.

notes.heading: Equivalent networks
notes.body: For linear resistive networks, use series/parallel reduction, source transformation, Thevenin, Norton, superposition, or nodal analysis only when the assumptions fit the circuit. Preserve the terminal behavior being analyzed.

notes.heading: Energy storage and checks
notes.body: Capacitors and inductors store energy and create time-dependent responses. Check units, limiting behavior, initial/final conditions, and whether a claimed steady-state result is physically consistent.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not add currents from different branches without a common node relationship, do not combine impedances as resistances in AC work, and do not use a source transformation without preserving polarity and terminal equivalence.

title: REE AC and Three-Phase Systems
summary: Source-first REE review of phasors, impedance, RMS conventions, AC power, resonance, and balanced three-phase relationships.

notes.heading: Phasor conventions
notes.body: Represent sinusoidal steady-state quantities with a declared RMS or peak convention. Add rectangular components consistently and interpret the sign of the angle as leading or lagging relative to the reference.

notes.heading: Impedance and power
notes.body: For series elements, resistance and reactance form a complex impedance. Use apparent power S, real power P, and reactive power Q consistently, with power factor describing the phase relationship rather than replacing the circuit model.

notes.heading: Three-phase assumptions
notes.body: For a balanced three-phase system, identify whether the stated voltage is line-to-line or line-to-neutral and whether the load is wye or delta before applying the square-root-of-three relationship.

notes.heading: Checks and limits
notes.body: Check units in VA, W, var, and ohms; test the resistive and purely reactive limiting cases; and state frequency, balance, and waveform assumptions when they affect the answer.

title: REE Machines and Transformers
summary: Source-first REE review of transformer ratios, electromechanical conversion, induction and synchronous speed, torque, losses, and efficiency.

notes.heading: Transformer model
notes.body: For an ideal transformer, voltage ratio follows turns ratio and current ratio is inverse when apparent power is conserved. Identify primary and secondary quantities and do not mix line and phase values without a stated connection.

notes.heading: Rotating-machine speed
notes.body: Synchronous speed depends on frequency and pole count. An induction motor operates below synchronous speed in motoring operation; slip is the normalized speed difference and must be interpreted with the stated operating mode.

notes.heading: Energy conversion
notes.body: Separate electrical input, mechanical output, losses, torque, and angular speed. Efficiency is useful output divided by input, and every power conversion question should state or expose the relevant loss assumption.

notes.heading: Prerequisite boundary
notes.body: These notes support foundational machine reasoning and calculations. Detailed design, saturation, fault behavior, and manufacturer/code-specific decisions require additional specialized sources and are not silently treated as generic reuse.

title: REE Power Systems and Distribution
summary: Source-first REE review of three-wire power, feeder performance, per-unit quantities, demand, diversity, losses, and system-level interpretation.

notes.heading: System model
notes.body: Start with the stated network model, voltage convention, phase count, and frequency. Distinguish load power, feeder loss, receiving-end power, and delivered energy before selecting a formula.

notes.heading: Per-unit reasoning
notes.body: Per-unit quantities normalize electrical values to a declared base. Keep voltage, current, impedance, and power bases consistent; a base change must transform the quantity rather than merely relabel it.

notes.heading: Demand and diversity
notes.body: Connected load, maximum demand, demand factor, and diversity factor answer different questions. Use the definition that matches the supplied data and do not assume all connected loads peak simultaneously.

notes.heading: Scope boundary
notes.body: These materials support stable power-system calculations and interpretation. Current Philippine code provisions, utility rules, protection settings, and regulatory thresholds require separately versioned authoritative sources and remain outside automatic reuse.

summary: Relays, interrupting ratings, grounding, converters, and feedback control.

title: REE Electronics Fundamentals
summary: Source-first REE review of diode models, amplifiers, filters, energy storage, semiconductor behavior, and basic conversion circuits.

notes.heading: Model selection
notes.body: Choose an ideal or piecewise-linear device model only when the question states or supports that approximation. Identify polarity, operating region, and reference ground before calculating.

notes.heading: Amplifiers and feedback
notes.body: An ideal operational-amplifier analysis commonly uses zero input current and equal input potentials under negative feedback, but verify that the circuit is operating in its linear region before applying those assumptions.

notes.heading: Filters and storage
notes.body: RC and RL networks have frequency- and time-dependent behavior. Relate cutoff and time constant to the component values, preserve units, and distinguish a transient response from sinusoidal steady state.

notes.heading: Sampling and conversion
notes.body: For an ideal n-bit converter spanning a stated voltage range, the nominal step is the span divided by 2^n equal levels. Distinguish quantization resolution from converter efficiency, and state the assumed range and ideal model before calculating.

notes.heading: Common mistakes
notes.body: Do not treat a diode as an always-on voltage source, confuse gain with output power, or ignore loading when a measurement or following stage changes the modeled circuit.

notes.heading: Batch 678 — Force on a current-carrying conductor
notes.body: Use F = B I L sin(θ). The conductor is perpendicular to the field, so sin(90°) = 1: (0.5 T)(4 A)(2 m) = 4 N. The units T·A·m reduce to newtons. Use a right-hand rule only when the force direction is requested.

title: REE Electrical Safety and Practice
summary: Hazard control, isolation, grounding purpose, and safe engineering decisions.

notes.heading: Use in practice
notes.body: Apply the relationships and decision checks to connect calculation results to safe electrical-engineering decisions.

notes.heading: Batch638 safety and source boundary
notes.body: Separate statutory workplace-safety duties from installation-code sizing rules. For an electrical hazard, keep people clear, arrange qualified isolation, and verify the work point is de-energized before contact. A calculated body-path current in a hypothetical is only an Ohm-law result; it is not a safe/unsafe threshold. RA 11058 supports the workplace-safety duty, while exact PEC limits require the controlling code text.

notes.heading: Application and common errors
notes.body: For safety scenarios, identify the hazard, the people exposed, the energy source, and the evidence that isolation is effective. Do not infer zero voltage from a switch position or tag alone; do not invent a code threshold from a general safety source. Explain why the proposed control addresses the hazard.

title: REE Electrical Design Applications

notes.heading: Use in practice
notes.body: Apply the relationships and decision checks to connect calculation results to safe electrical-engineering decisions.

notes.heading: Batch638 design-data boundary
notes.body: Separate arithmetic from code-dependent design decisions. A connected-load sum is not automatically maximum demand; a computed voltage drop is not a declaration of code compliance unless the governing edition, installation conditions, and applicable limit are supplied. Interpret illumination at the task plane rather than substituting lamp wattage for delivered illuminance.

notes.heading: Application checks
notes.body: For a schedule or layout, verify the listed quantities, units, operating assumptions, route conditions, and interface constraints before drawing a conclusion. Treat a missing diversity factor or code limit as missing evidence, not as permission to assume a preferred value.

title: REE Integrated Engineering Review
summary: Integrated calculations and diagnostic reasoning across the REE scope.

notes.heading: Use in practice
notes.body: Apply the relationships and decision checks to connect calculation results to safe electrical-engineering decisions.

notes.heading: Batch638 protection and currentness boundary
notes.body: Distinguish stable protection principles (fault detection, selective coordination, backup protection, current-transformer scaling, and interruption) from version-sensitive equipment selection. In a simplified question, state any assumed comparison rule in the stem. Do not assert a PEC conductor size, breaker value, grounding dimension, or PGC 2026 requirement without the controlling adopted text. ERC material reviewed for this batch identifies the approved PGC 2016 edition and separately labels the 2026 edition as a draft under consultation.

notes.heading: Worked reasoning and common errors
notes.body: For a coordination scenario, first identify the faulted zone and the intended primary device; then check whether a backup remains available if the primary fails. For a rating comparison, compare like quantities and explicitly state the assumed inequality. Avoid treating relay time alone as proof of full coordination or using a grid-code draft as current law.

title: Architectural Precedent and Spatial Order
summary: Evidence-based architectural precedent and spatial-order review for interpreting axes, hierarchy, rhythm, proportion, circulation, and transformation without reducing history to labels.

notes.heading: Reading precedent
notes.body: Read a precedent through observable relationships: approach, threshold, enclosure, axis, hierarchy, proportion, repetition, structure, material, and use. A style name is a starting hypothesis, not proof of the design logic.

notes.heading: Spatial order
notes.body: An axis organizes movement or visual emphasis; hierarchy distinguishes primary from secondary spaces; rhythm repeats a feature with a readable interval; datum and proportion relate parts without requiring literal copying.

notes.heading: Design transfer
notes.body: When adapting a precedent, retain the underlying spatial operation that answers the new program. Copying ornament while destroying circulation, climate response, or public/private hierarchy is not faithful transformation.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not infer a period solely from ornament, treat symmetry as the only ordering device, or assume a contemporary intervention is incompatible because it is visibly new. Explain the evidence and the consequence.

title: Vernacular and Climate-Responsive Traditions
summary: Climate-responsive and vernacular architecture review linking climate, culture, material practice, settlement pattern, and passive environmental response.

notes.heading: Climate as evidence
notes.body: Start with sun, wind, rainfall, humidity, temperature swing, ground conditions, and available materials. A response is climate-responsive only when its geometry, openings, shade, mass, or ventilation addresses a stated condition.

notes.heading: Vernacular reasoning
notes.body: Vernacular forms encode accumulated adaptation, labor, material availability, social practice, and local hazard knowledge. Transfer principles and performance logic; do not treat a form as a universal decorative template.

notes.heading: Passive strategies
notes.body: Orientation, shading, cross-ventilation, stack effect, thermal mass, daylight control, and rain protection interact. A strategy can improve one variable while worsening glare, heat gain, moisture, security, or maintenance.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not equate more glass with daylight, open windows with useful ventilation, or a familiar vernacular image with a verified climate response. State the climate and user assumptions before choosing.

title: Conservation and Adaptive Reuse Reasoning
summary: Conservation and adaptive-reuse review for significance, documentation, character-defining fabric, compatible change, reversibility, and performance upgrades.

notes.heading: Significance and documentation
notes.body: Before intervention, document history, condition, materials, alterations, character-defining spaces, views, details, and evidence uncertainty. A treatment cannot be judged responsibly without knowing what matters and why.

notes.heading: Compatible change
notes.body: Good adaptive reuse retains significant character, repairs before replacing, distinguishes new work without competing with the historic resource, and makes necessary changes as compatible and as reversible as practical.

notes.heading: Performance upgrades
notes.body: Accessibility, life safety, moisture control, and energy improvements are legitimate design drivers. Coordinate them with existing fabric; a visually hidden intervention can still cause condensation, trapped moisture, or structural damage.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not freeze a building regardless of safety, reconstruct undocumented details as fact, or erase evidence of change merely to create a false original appearance.

notes: Batch 680 — Accessible reuse in a historic market

Document significance and character-defining fabric before intervention. Provide an accessible route that meets the current BP 344 IRR; the 2024 IRR specifies a 1200 mm minimum clear ramp width and a 1:20 general maximum gradient, with limited special cases and additional landing/handrail requirements. Coordinate the route with significant fabric and use compatible, reversible work where practicable; accessibility remains a required design outcome.

title: Architectural Scope and Decision Records
summary: Professional practice review for scope, authorization, decision records, assumptions, deliverables, and responsibility boundaries in architectural services.

notes.heading: Scope and authorization
notes.body: Identify the service, deliverable, decision authority, constraints, exclusions, and required specialist input before acting. A design preference is not authorization to change scope, budget, or compliance obligations.

notes.heading: Decision records
notes.body: A useful record states the issue, reliable facts, alternatives considered, assumptions, responsible parties, consequences, and approval. It lets a later reviewer distinguish an informed decision from an undocumented guess.

notes.heading: Practice boundary
notes.body: RA 9266 identifies architectural services and professional responsibility boundaries. Questions use the law for scope reasoning and do not infer a legal conclusion where the supplied facts or current implementing rule is incomplete.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not transfer an unresolved professional decision silently, conceal a limitation, or treat a consultant recommendation as self-executing without checking scope, coordination, and authorization.

title: Consultant Coordination and Change Control
summary: Consultant coordination and change-control review for interfaces, information versions, submittals, constructability, schedule, cost, and authorized project change.

notes.heading: Interface control
notes.body: Coordinate architectural intent with structure, enclosure, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, fire/life safety, site, and specialty systems at the interface where geometry and responsibility meet.

notes.heading: Information status
notes.body: Confirm the current drawing/specification revision, design assumption, field condition, and decision authority before issuing or relying on information. A marked-up sheet is not automatically an authorized change.

notes.heading: Change reasoning
notes.body: Evaluate a proposed change for design intent, code/life-safety effect, constructability, cost, schedule, maintenance, and downstream coordination. Record the decision and update affected documents.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not resolve a clash by moving the visible object only, ignore access and maintenance zones, or issue conflicting instructions to trades without a controlled record.

title: Professional Judgment and Public Responsibility
summary: Professional judgment review for competence, public safety, accessibility, confidentiality, impartiality, risk communication, and defensible architectural decisions.

notes.heading: Public responsibility
notes.body: Architectural judgment must account for occupants, users with disabilities, public safety, durability, and foreseeable consequences—not only client preference or first cost.

notes.heading: Competence and referral
notes.body: Recognize when a question exceeds the architect’s competent scope and obtain qualified specialist input. Coordination preserves architectural responsibility; it does not mean adopting an unreviewed recommendation.

notes.heading: Communication
notes.body: State uncertainty, assumptions, risks, and affected parties plainly. Preserve confidential information while disclosing material safety or compliance concerns through the proper channel.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not hide a known risk to protect schedule, accept a conflict without disclosure, or call a code-sensitive choice neutral when the regulatory requirement materially controls the answer.

title: Envelope, Moisture, Thermal, and Acoustic Assemblies
summary: Building-envelope and assembly review for water, air, vapor, thermal, acoustic, structural, and maintainability control layers.

notes.heading: Control layers
notes.body: Trace water, air, vapor, thermal, and structural control continuously across roofs, walls, openings, foundations, joints, and penetrations. Continuity and drainage matter more than naming a single “best” material.

notes.heading: Moisture
notes.body: Provide a shedding surface, drainage path, flashing, compatible transitions, drying potential, and maintainable joints. Condensation risk depends on temperature, humidity, air leakage, vapor movement, and layer location.

notes.heading: Thermal and acoustic behavior
notes.body: Thermal bridges bypass insulation; acoustic flanking bypasses a nominal partition rating. Use continuity, isolation, mass, absorptive treatment, and sealed penetrations as appropriate to the source of transmission.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not rely on sealant as the only water strategy, put a vapor-control assumption into a different climate without checking, or close an assembly before inspection and drainage paths are resolved.

title: Water, Drainage, Ventilation, and Electrical Coordination
summary: Building-utilities coordination review for water, drainage, ventilation, electrical, fire/life safety, access, clearances, and serviceability.

notes.heading: System coordination
notes.body: Reserve shafts, ceiling zones, plant rooms, risers, access panels, equipment clearances, drainage falls, and fire separations before the architectural plan is fixed. Each system has a path, a space claim, and a maintenance need.

notes.heading: Water and drainage
notes.body: Flow requires a connected route, adequate gradient or pumping strategy, cleanouts, access, overflow logic, and protection of occupied spaces. A fixture count alone does not establish a workable drainage layout.

notes.heading: Ventilation and electrical
notes.body: Ventilation design balances air path, pressure, noise, filtration, heat, and maintenance. Electrical coordination distinguishes power, controls, emergency systems, equipment heat, working clearances, and fire/life-safety interfaces.

notes.heading: Regulatory boundary
notes.body: Current code and accessibility sources govern regulated thresholds and approvals. When a question does not provide the current jurisdictional value, choose the coordination principle rather than inventing a number.

title: Construction Quantities, Sequencing, and Interfaces
summary: Construction and material-technology review for quantities, tolerances, sequencing, joints, constructability, procurement, inspection, and interface risk.

notes.heading: Quantities and units
notes.body: Separate gross and net area, volume, count, waste allowance, and unit rate. State thickness and unit system before calculating; a quantity is only useful when its measurement basis is explicit.

notes.heading: Sequence and tolerances
notes.body: Sequence work so wet trades cure, concealed work is inspected, interfaces remain accessible, and tolerances accumulate within the intended fit. The nominal dimension is not the same as the installable dimension.

notes.heading: Material compatibility
notes.body: Check movement, moisture, corrosion, galvanic contact, fire behavior, sealant compatibility, fasteners, and maintenance. A strong material can fail when the joint or adjacent material is incompatible.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not measure a void as finished area, close a wall before testing concealed utilities, or treat a shop drawing as permission to change a design without review.

title: Site Climate, Orientation, and Environmental Response
summary: Site climate and environmental-response review for solar exposure, wind, rainfall, contours, vegetation, noise, views, microclimate, and passive design.

notes.heading: Site evidence
notes.body: Map sun, prevailing wind, topography, drainage, vegetation, noise, views, access, adjacent uses, hazards, and existing infrastructure before placing major functions. The site is a set of relationships, not a blank polygon.

notes.heading: Orientation and form
notes.body: Orient openings, mass, shade, outdoor space, and circulation in response to climate and use. The best solar orientation for one façade may produce glare, heat, or poor cross-ventilation elsewhere.

notes.heading: Water and terrain
notes.body: Follow contours and natural drainage where possible, minimize unnecessary cut/fill, protect soil and vegetation, and direct runoff without creating a downstream nuisance or undermining foundations.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not rotate a plan for a diagrammatic ideal while ignoring wind or access, treat north as the only solar datum, or specify a passive strategy without stating occupancy and climate assumptions.

notes.heading: Worked site schedule: daylight, glare, shade, and arrival
notes.body: For the stated reading-room schedule, compare late-afternoon sun at the west edge with shade at the north edge, then test a north-side location and shading against daylight and glare needs while keeping the east arrival legible. This is a response to supplied site facts, not a universal orientation rule.

title: Circulation, Adjacency, and Functional Zoning
summary: Spatial programming review for adjacency, circulation, public/private/service separation, accessibility, egress logic, wayfinding, and functional zoning.

notes.heading: Adjacency
notes.body: Translate activities, users, privacy, noise, service, security, sequence, and time of use into relationships before drawing rooms. A bubble diagram is a reasoning device, not a finished plan.

notes.heading: Circulation
notes.body: Separate and then coordinate public, private, service, accessible, emergency, and vehicular movement. A short path is not automatically a good path if it conflicts with safety, orientation, or dignity.

notes.heading: Accessibility and life safety
notes.body: Accessibility and egress are design constraints that shape entries, routes, doors, level changes, and refuge/exit logic. Use current official requirements for dimensions and approvals; this material supports reasoning, not invented code values.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not place rooms by visual symmetry alone, hide service movement in a user route, or call a plan accessible because a route exists without checking continuity, maneuvering, and usable facilities.

notes.heading: 2024 accessible-route audit
notes.body: The 2024 BP 344 IRR defines an accessible route as continuous and unobstructed, connecting accessible elements and spaces. It requires public entrances to be accessible from arrival and departure points to the interior lobby, without longer travel or exclusion from the standard path. Trace the entire trip across site arrival, entries, doors, level changes, and interior destinations; then verify each dimension against the IRR. A route that exists on the plan but breaks at a segment is not continuous.

notes.heading: Worked site schedule: follow the route end to end
notes.body: If the direct line from arrival crosses steps but a level path reaches the accessible entrance and lobby, trace the level path through every segment to the destination. Check continuity, obstructions, and applicable dimensional requirements against the 2024 BP 344 IRR. A line that stops at the site edge is not a complete route.

title: Site Capacity, Growth, and Spatial Alternatives
summary: Site-capacity and spatial-alternatives review for footprint, coverage, buffers, growth, landscape, infrastructure, wayfinding, and competing site consequences.

notes.heading: Capacity
notes.body: Compare alternatives using the stated site area, buildable envelope, access, setbacks or buffers, landscape, drainage, servicing, user capacity, and future change—not footprint alone.

notes.heading: Growth and phasing
notes.body: A robust master plan reserves logical expansion zones, keeps essential circulation and utilities serviceable, protects future fire/access paths, and avoids making the first phase impossible to adapt.

notes.heading: Trade-offs
notes.body: Every alternative redistributes impacts: compactness may preserve landscape but increase height or servicing intensity; a dispersed plan may reduce height but increase infrastructure and travel. State the criterion before choosing.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not maximize floor area while ignoring stormwater, access, public realm, or future operations, and do not treat a single compliance check as proof that the whole site strategy is sound.

title: Philippine Civil Code: Obligations, Contracts, Sales, and Remedies
summary: Concept-fit legal foundation for contract formation, obligations, sales, validity, remedies, and partnership relationships under the Philippine Civil Code.

notes.heading: Application boundary
notes.body: Analyze the supplied consent, authority, performance, breach, and remedy facts before drawing a legal conclusion. Do not treat a general label or a business practice as proof of a statutory result.

notes.heading: Contracts and obligations
notes.body: Use the parties' assent, definite subject, consideration, contractual terms, and timing to evaluate formation and performance. Separate a contractual obligation from a remedy that may follow a proven breach.

notes.heading: Sales and remedies
notes.body: Use the supplied delivery, conformity, notice, and defect facts to identify the next legally supported response. A remedy depends on the contract and applicable law; avoid unsupported absolute outcomes.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes are a concise study aid based on Republic Act No. 386. Consult the primary text and applicable jurisprudence for the complete rule and exceptions.

title: Philippine Corporate Authority and Governance
summary: Technical study foundation for corporate powers, board authority, share transactions, formalities, and governance decisions.

notes.heading: Authority and governance
notes.body: Distinguish the corporation's separate legal authority from the internal approval and documentation required by its governing documents and applicable law. Verify authority and ratification rather than assuming a management signature is sufficient.

notes.heading: Corporate transactions
notes.body: Analyze the stated board action, shareholder or officer role, transaction purpose, and conflict facts. Do not infer a current statutory threshold or approval rule unless the source and facts supply it.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes summarize selected applications of Republic Act No. 11232 and are not a substitute for the statute, implementing rules, or official guidance.

title: Negotiable Instruments and Commercial Security
summary: Concept-fit support for negotiable-instrument status, presentment, notice, defenses, and priority analysis.

notes.heading: Instrument analysis
notes.body: Start with the instrument's form, transfer, value, good faith, notice, and presentment facts. Separate holder status from the ultimate enforceability or priority conclusion.

notes.heading: Evidence and defenses
notes.body: A favorable holder-status fact does not erase every defense or procedural requirement. Identify the supplied issue and apply the relevant statutory condition without adding unstated facts.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes summarize selected applications of Act No. 2031. Consult the primary Negotiable Instruments Law for complete requirements and exceptions.

title: Philippine Accountancy Practice, Records, and Confidentiality
summary: Professional and statutory foundation for accountancy practice, working papers, records, confidentiality, disclosure, and professional responsibility.

notes.heading: Professional scope
notes.body: Apply the Accountancy Act and professional standards to the supplied role, document, and duty facts. Do not treat every business record as a privileged document or every request as an automatic disclosure exception.

notes.heading: Records and confidentiality
notes.body: Distinguish ownership and retention of working papers, client authorization, lawful compulsory production, and other professional duties. The correct response should preserve evidence and state the applicable limitation accurately.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes are based on Republic Act No. 9298 and the Philippine professional ethics adoption material. Consult the primary law and current professional requirements for complete treatment.

title: Professional Ethics, Conflicts, and Disclosure
summary: Application-focused support for integrity, objectivity, conflicts of interest, authorized disclosure, and independent decision-making.

notes.heading: Conflict analysis
notes.body: Identify the threat to integrity or objectivity, disclose the relevant relationship, and evaluate safeguards or independent review. A conflict signal requires analysis; it does not by itself prove misconduct.

notes.heading: Disclosure decisions
notes.body: Separate authorized disclosure, disclosure required by law or professional duty, and inappropriate disclosure. State the facts needed for a conclusion rather than inventing an exception.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes are based on the Philippine Code of Ethics adoption material and Republic Act No. 9298. They are a study aid, not a replacement for the current professional code.

title: Agency: Authority, Ratification, and Principal-Agent Effects
summary: Concept-fit Philippine agency-law foundation for evaluating representation, express and implied authority, ratification, and the effect of known authority limits on the principal.

notes.heading: Agency and authority
notes.body: Analyze whether a person acts in representation with the principal's consent or authority. Distinguish express authority, implied authority from conduct, and a third party's knowledge of an express limit before concluding whether the principal is bound.

notes.heading: Ratification
notes.body: When an unauthorized act is presented, assess the principal's subsequent conduct and acceptance of the benefit under the governing agency provisions. Acceptance may support ratification, but the conclusion remains tied to the supplied facts and applicable law.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: These notes are a concise study aid based on the cited Philippine Civil Code provisions; consult the primary text for the complete rule and exceptions.

title: Philippine Taxable Income, Bases, Deductions, and Exclusions
summary: Concept-fit support for tracing receipts and adjustments to the supplied taxable base while separating substantiation, deductions, exclusions, and period assumptions.

notes.heading: Build the tax base
notes.body: Start with the taxpayer and period, identify included receipts, then apply only the deductions or exclusions supported by the facts and governing rule. A supplied exercise rate is not evidence of a current statutory rate.

notes.heading: Substantiation and reconciliation
notes.body: Reconcile accounting records to the tax schedule and verify documentary support before accepting an adjustment. Keep recognition, classification, and computation as separate decisions.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: Use the current National Internal Revenue Code and applicable BIR issuances for live-law rates, thresholds, effective dates, and exceptions.

title: Philippine Business Taxes, VAT, and Withholding Analysis
summary: Concept-fit support for separating VAT output/input analysis, withholding roles, business-tax classification, and supplied transaction data.

notes.heading: Classify before computing
notes.body: Identify the transaction, taxpayer role, tax base, and whether an amount is output tax, input credit, withholding, or a separate business tax before calculating.

notes.heading: Withholding and VAT
notes.body: A withholding agent's remittance obligation and the payee's tax position are related but not interchangeable. Follow the applicable current Code section and BIR issuance.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: Current rates and digital-service rules require the current Tax Code amendments and BIR implementation guidance.

title: Philippine Transfer Taxes and Exemption Analysis
summary: Concept-fit support for estate and donor transfer-tax bases, exclusions, documentary evidence, and fact-specific exemption analysis.

notes.heading: Construct the transfer base
notes.body: Separate the gross transfer or estate value from deductions and legally supported exclusions. Do not assume that a label such as gift or inheritance resolves the tax treatment without checking the transaction facts.

notes.heading: Evidence matters
notes.body: Use the stated ownership, date, relationship, valuation, and documentary facts; unsupported exemptions should be investigated rather than applied automatically.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: Transfer-tax rates, thresholds, and exemptions are time-sensitive and must be checked against the current Code and BIR issuances.

title: Philippine Tax Filing, Records, Administration, and Remedies
summary: Concept-fit support for registration, filing, records, assessments, taxpayer responses, substantiation, and administrative remedies.

notes.heading: Procedural sequence
notes.body: First identify the notice, taxpayer action, controlling period, and procedural record. Then determine the available response under the current Code and implementing issuance; do not infer a deadline from an unstated fact.

notes.heading: Records and substantiation
notes.body: A return, invoice, ledger, and supporting document answer different evidentiary questions. Preserve the record and reconcile inconsistencies before recommending a filing or protest response.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: Use the National Internal Revenue Code, current BIR issuances, and official filing instructions for live procedural requirements.

title: Philippine Tax Research, Ethics, and Current-Law Controls
summary: Concept-fit support for researching current tax authority, documenting assumptions, handling uncertainty, and maintaining professional judgment in tax work.

notes.heading: Current-law control
notes.body: A technically correct calculation under an old rate or period is not a current-law conclusion. Record the effective date, authority level, and assumptions used.

notes.heading: Professional judgment
notes.body: When records conflict or the law is unsettled, identify the missing authority, escalate appropriately, and avoid presenting an unsupported absolute answer to a client.

notes.heading: Source boundary
notes.body: The BIR Tax Code page, current BIR issuances, and official filing materials are the starting points; secondary summaries require verification.

title: LET English Reading and Evidence Foundation
summary: Source-backed LET reading practice for main ideas, inference, evidence, purpose, tone, context clues, and text structure.

notes.heading: Evidence before inference
notes.body: Separate what a passage states from what it supports by implication. A defensible inference uses multiple relevant details and does not add outside knowledge.

notes.heading: Central idea and support
notes.body: A central idea accounts for the passage as a whole; supporting details explain, illustrate, qualify, or provide evidence for it.

notes.heading: Purpose, tone, and structure
notes.body: Purpose is the writer's communicative goal, tone is the attitude conveyed by language, and structure describes how ideas relate or develop.

notes.heading: Context and critical reading
notes.body: Use contrast, examples, definitions, and surrounding relationships to interpret words. Evaluate claims by asking whether the evidence supports the strength of the conclusion.

title: LET English Grammar and Sentence Revision Foundation
summary: Technical LET English foundation for contextual sentence revision across structure, agreement, tense, modifiers, pronouns, parallelism, prepositions, and parts of speech.

notes.heading: Sentence structure
notes.body: Distinguish independent and dependent clauses, then use coordination or subordination to express the intended relationship. Repair fragments, run-ons, and comma splices without changing the meaning.

notes.heading: Agreement and verb form
notes.body: Locate the grammatical subject rather than the nearest noun. Select verb forms and tense sequences that match number, time, aspect, and the relationship among actions.

notes.heading: Modifiers and reference
notes.body: Place modifiers beside the words they logically describe and supply a clear subject for introductory phrases. Check pronoun antecedent, number, and case so the intended referent is recoverable.

notes.heading: Parallelism and usage
notes.body: Keep coordinated items grammatically equivalent, compare like forms, and choose prepositions according to the stated relationship. Evaluate parts of speech by the word’s function in its sentence, not by its spelling alone.

title: CPA Financial Accounting and Reporting: Evidence-to-Statement Reasoning
summary: Source-backed FAR study resource for recognition, measurement, presentation, estimates, and financial-statement consequences.

notes.heading: Framework and presentation
notes.body: Use the Conceptual Framework and applicable presentation standard to identify the element, recognition evidence, measurement basis, classification, and statement effect. Relevance and faithful representation are distinct qualitative characteristics; a convenient number is not automatically a valid measurement.

notes.heading: Assets and liabilities
notes.body: For inventory, receivables, PPE, intangibles, provisions, and leases, separate initial recognition from subsequent measurement. State the supplied assumptions, identify the applicable basis, and trace the result to profit, equity, assets, or liabilities.

notes.heading: Timing and estimates
notes.body: Accruals and events after the reporting period require a reporting-date analysis. A change in estimate is prospective; a material prior-period error is corrected under the applicable presentation requirements. Do not treat every later event as adjusting.

notes.heading: Common errors
notes.body: Do not use cash timing as a substitute for accrual recognition, mix output and input amounts, omit directly attributable costs, or infer a standard treatment from an account label alone.

title: CPA Advanced Financial Accounting: Consolidation, Partnership, and Arrangement Evidence
summary: Source-backed advanced-accounting resource for control, acquisition method, partnerships, branches, joint arrangements, foreign exchange, and separate reporting.

notes.heading: Control and acquisition
notes.body: Distinguish control from percentage ownership, identify acquired assets and liabilities at the applicable measurement basis, and keep consideration, net assets, goodwill, NCI, and consolidation adjustments separate.

notes.heading: Partnership and liquidation
notes.body: Apply the stated partnership agreement and liquidation method to capital balances, admission, withdrawal, profit allocation, claim priority, and settlement. Do not import corporate rules into a partnership fact pattern.

notes.heading: Branches and arrangements
notes.body: Reconcile reciprocal accounts before preparing combined statements. Classify a joint operation by rights and obligations, not by the label in the contract, and distinguish a joint venture from a business combination.

notes.heading: Currency and separate statements
notes.body: Keep transaction remeasurement, translation, equity-method accounting, and separate-financial-statement measurement distinct. State the rate and reporting assumption used.

notes.heading: Goodwill: identify every acquisition-date input
notes.body: IFRS 3 measures goodwill as consideration transferred plus any non-controlling interest plus the acquisition-date fair value of a previously held interest, less the acquisition-date net amount of identifiable assets acquired and liabilities assumed. A simple consideration-minus-net-assets exercise is valid only when the vignette excludes the additional interests and adjustments. Reassess measurements before recognizing a bargain-purchase gain.

title: CPA Management Services: Decision and Performance Evidence
summary: Open-text-supported management-accounting resource for cost behavior, CVP, budgets, variances, relevant decisions, ABC, and capital budgeting.

notes.heading: Decision relevance
notes.body: Include future amounts that differ between alternatives, including opportunity costs when capacity is scarce. Exclude sunk and unavoidable allocated costs unless the question supplies a reason they change.

notes.heading: CVP and mix
notes.body: Contribution margin is sales less variable cost. Preserve the stated product mix when computing weighted contribution or break-even; a volume change, price change, or fixed-cost change has a different sensitivity implication.

notes.heading: Budgets and variances
notes.body: Separate operating income from cash timing. Identify the standard and actual basis before calculating a variance, then interpret it as a signal for investigation rather than proof of responsibility.

notes.heading: ABC and investment
notes.body: Calculate each activity-pool rate from its stated driver, and keep payback, present value, and NPV distinct. Allocation is an analytical model, not automatically a cash outflow.

title: CPA Auditing: Risk, Evidence, Procedures, and Reporting
summary: Currentness-aware auditing resource for assertions, risk, controls, evidence, analytical procedures, sampling, documentation, going concern, fraud, and reporting.

notes.heading: Risk and controls
notes.body: Understand the entity and its controls before selecting responses. Inherent risk, control risk, and detection risk are related but not interchangeable; a control deficiency does not by itself establish a financial-statement misstatement.

notes.heading: Evidence and procedures
notes.body: Evaluate evidence for sufficiency and appropriateness, including relevance and reliability. Match the procedure to the assertion and risk; an external confirmation can be strong evidence for one assertion without answering every assertion.

notes.heading: Analysis and sampling
notes.body: Develop an expectation for analytical procedures, investigate significant unexplained differences, and evaluate sampling results using the stated population, sample, and projection assumptions.

notes.heading: Reporting and documentation
notes.body: Classify a misstatement or scope limitation by materiality and pervasiveness before selecting the report consequence. Documentation should allow an experienced auditor to understand the work, evidence, and conclusion. Current Philippine adoption and effective dates control standard-sensitive claims.

notes: Batch 680 — Match evidence to the assertion

An external confirmation about a customer receivable may support that receivable’s existence; it does not establish that all supplier liabilities were recorded. Identify the liability-completeness risk, choose evidence directed to recorded and potentially omitted obligations, and evaluate relevance and reliability before concluding.

title: CPA Regulatory Framework: Philippine Law, Governance, and Professional Responsibility
summary: Primary-law-supported CPA resource for obligations, contracts, sales, agency, corporations, negotiable instruments, partnerships, records, confidentiality, and conflicts.

notes.heading: Fact-bound legal analysis
notes.body: Identify consent, authority, object, consideration, performance, notice, breach, and remedy facts before drawing a legal conclusion. A general business label cannot replace the facts required by the governing law.

notes.heading: Corporate and agency authority
notes.body: Separate the corporation’s legal personality from internal approval and documentation. For agency, distinguish express authority, implied authority, notice of a limit, and ratification.

notes.heading: Professional responsibility
notes.body: Apply the Accountancy Act and current Philippine ethics adoption material to records, confidentiality, conflicts, objectivity, and lawful disclosure. State missing facts rather than inventing an exception.

notes.heading: Version boundary
notes.body: Statutes and professional rules are version-sensitive. The primary text and current Philippine adoption control; these notes are concise instructional support, not a substitute for the law or code.

title: CPA Taxation: Philippine Tax Base, Compliance, and Current-Law Controls
summary: Current-source-aware tax resource for tax-base construction, deductions, VAT, withholding, filing, records, exemptions, administration, and professional research.

notes.heading: Build before computing
notes.body: Identify the taxpayer, transaction, period, tax base, and legal role before applying an amount. A rate supplied by an exercise is a calculation assumption, not proof of a current statutory rate.

notes.heading: Evidence and reconciliation
notes.body: Reconcile books, schedules, returns, invoices, and supporting documents. Keep recognition, classification, substantiation, and arithmetic as separate decisions.

notes.heading: VAT and withholding
notes.body: Output tax, input credit, withholding, remittance, and the payee’s tax position are related but not interchangeable. Follow the current Tax Code and BIR issuance for live rates, thresholds, forms, and effective dates.

notes.heading: Current-law control
notes.body: Record the effective period and authority level. If a client asks for a current rate or filing rule, verify the current BIR issuance rather than relying on memory or an old summary.

title: Batch 625 NP I: Community Clinical Reasoning
summary: Apply population assessment, prevention, epidemiology, teaching, disaster planning, and equity reasoning to a community nursing decision.

notes.heading: Assessment
notes.body: Define the population, verify the pattern, identify immediate threats, and distinguish missing information from an established finding.

notes.heading: Action and monitoring
notes.body: Select a feasible least-harm intervention, protect privacy, use current program guidance, document the response, and evaluate outcomes rather than activity alone.

notes.heading: Teaching and equity
notes.body: Use plain language, qualified interpretation, teach-back, culturally responsive planning, and proportional resource allocation.

notes.heading: Boundary
notes.body: A useful science foundation does not itself establish an independent Nursing coverage row; keep shared-science claims separate from NP I competency evidence.

notes.heading: Outbreak investigation: verify before attributing
notes.body: Confirm the reported diagnosis and assess whether the observed count exceeds an appropriate baseline; define and count cases systematically, then describe patterns by time, place, and person. Early steps may occur concurrently. Use required reporting channels, protect identifiable records, and do not announce a cause before evidence supports it. CDC Field Epi Manual.

title: Batch 625 NP II: Maternal, Newborn, and Family Decisions
summary: Connect maternal, labor, postpartum, newborn, growth, development, and family cues to safe assessment, escalation, teaching, and referral.

notes.heading: Assessment
notes.body: Cluster maternal and newborn findings, compare trends with baseline, identify danger signs, and avoid unsupported absolute claims.

notes.heading: Time-sensitive care
notes.body: Use current local protocols for fetal, maternal, newborn, infection, medication, and resuscitation decisions; escalate instability promptly.

notes.heading: Family partnership
notes.body: Respect consent, privacy, language, culture, and family participation while retaining professional accountability for safe care.

notes.heading: Teaching
notes.body: Use demonstration and teach-back for feeding, warning signs, medication, wound, and follow-up instructions.

title: Batch 625 NP III: Medical-Surgical Safety Decisions
summary: Interpret acute and chronic oxygenation, fluid, infection, immune, perioperative, and cellular cues through assessment, intervention, monitoring, and escalation.

notes.heading: Stability first
notes.body: Use airway, breathing, circulation, mental status, trend, and response to distinguish deterioration from a stable finding.

notes.heading: Infection safety
notes.body: Apply standard precautions, transmission-based measures, aseptic practice, source control, and current local policy.

notes.heading: Perioperative care
notes.body: Verify identity, consent, allergies, procedure, orders, equipment, and postoperative response; never substitute a checklist for assessment.

notes.heading: Monitoring
notes.body: Reassess after an intervention and escalate when the supplied facts show actual deterioration or an unresolved safety threat.

title: Batch 625 NP IV: Nutrition, Endocrine, Coordination, and Medication Safety
summary: Relate nutrition, gastrointestinal, endocrine, perceptual, coordination, and medication cues to individualized nursing decisions and monitoring.

notes.heading: Assessment
notes.body: Use intake, output, function, trends, symptoms, treatment, and patient goals instead of treating an isolated number as a diagnosis.

notes.heading: Medication safety
notes.body: Verify the complete order, patient, product, indication, route, allergies, units, monitoring, teaching, and response; clarify uncertainty before administration.

notes.heading: Coordination
notes.body: Match delegation and handoff to acuity, competence, scope, and accountability; use closed-loop communication and factual documentation.

notes.heading: Currentness
notes.body: Use current medication and local clinical guidance for time-sensitive care; stable fundamentals remain stable and are not artificially versioned.

title: Batch 625 NP V: Mental Health, Emergency, and High-Acuity Decisions
summary: Prioritize maladaptive behavior, crisis, shock, acute multi-organ problems, emergency care, teamwork, and escalation using the supplied facts.

notes.heading: Immediate safety
notes.body: Stay with an unsafe patient, assess immediate risk, reduce hazards, and activate urgent support rather than promising secrecy or waiting.

notes.heading: Emergency reasoning
notes.body: Use a systematic ABCDE/SAMPLE approach, stabilize within role and protocol, reassess response, and communicate changes clearly.

notes.heading: Acuity and delegation
notes.body: Prioritize actual instability and new deterioration; retain assessment and evaluation accountability for high-risk patients.

notes.heading: Therapeutic care
notes.body: Use nonjudgmental communication, privacy, informed participation, least-restrictive safety measures, and current referral guidance.

notes: Learning objectives
