title: Prestressed Concrete Foundations for CELE Review
summary: Source-first Civil Engineering study foundation for basic prestressing principles, construction sequence, stress resultants, losses, and service behavior within current CELE scope.
notes: Purpose and scope

Prestressing introduces a controlled compression pattern to offset part of the tensile response from service actions. The CELE-level treatment is conceptual and application-oriented; it does not assume specialist bridge detailing.
Pretensioning and post-tensioning

Pretensioned tendons are stressed before concrete placement and transfer occurs after the concrete reaches the required condition. Post-tensioned tendons are stressed after concrete placement and use anchorages and the specified duct or tendon system.
Section stress behavior

For a simple average stress check, prestressing force is divided by the relevant area. An eccentric force also creates a force-couple moment. Sign convention and tendon location must be stated before interpreting compression or tension at a fiber.
Loss mechanisms

Elastic shortening, creep, shrinkage, steel relaxation, anchorage seating, and friction or wobble effects where applicable can reduce effective prestress. A question must identify which losses are supplied and avoid double counting.
Service implications
Prestressing can reduce service tensile stress and cracking tendency, but service stress, deflection, durability, anchorage, and construction-stage behavior still require separate checks.
Common errors
Do not treat initial jacking force as effective service force, confuse pretensioning with post-tensioning, or claim that prestressing guarantees zero cracking or deflection.

title: Governing Structural Codes and Currentness for CELE Review
summary: Study foundation for distinguishing the current CELE scope authority, stable engineering principles, version-sensitive requirements, and defensible code-based application.
notes: Authority hierarchy

The current PRC CELE program establishes examination scope. A recognized project code, regulation, or official authority controls a version-sensitive design requirement; instructional notes explain principles but do not replace that authority.
Stable principle versus requirement

Equilibrium, load path, strength behavior, and serviceability concepts can be taught as stable principles. Numerical limits, factors, editions, and jurisdiction-specific requirements must be tied to the current controlling source.
Application reading
Interpret a code-based question by identifying the member, action, limit state, material, jurisdiction, edition, and supplied factors before selecting an answer.
Documentation
A defensible engineering decision records the controlling source and version or retrieval date, states assumptions, and distinguishes an official requirement from a study simplification.
Common errors
Avoid undated section-number trivia, silently averaging conflicting requirements, treating a textbook shortcut as a code rule, or using a value outside its stated scope.

title: REE Mathematics — Trigonometry and Analytic Geometry
summary: Angle/period relationships, trigonometric functions and identities, polar/Cartesian representation, vectors and analytic geometry with engineering interpretation.

notes.heading: Core ideas
notes.body: Represent angles with explicit units and reference direction. Use unit-circle signs, identities, law of sines/cosines, polar and Cartesian coordinates, vectors, lines and conics when appropriate. In phasor-style questions state whether degrees or radians are used and preserve quadrant information.

notes.heading: Worked check
notes.body: For 12∠30°, x=12 cos 30°≈10.39 and y=12 sin 30°=6.00, so the rectangular form is approximately 10.39+j6.00. Check magnitude with √(x²+y²) and use the original quadrant to determine the angle.

notes.heading: Common errors and application
notes.body: Common errors include calculator mode mismatch, losing the sign of a component, using the wrong inverse-trigonometric quadrant, and confusing a slope with an angle. Prefer interpretation/application questions with explicit geometry; keep the math within PRC-listed scope.

registered-electrical-engineering.rationale: PRC-listed trigonometry and analytic geometry; stable mathematical reasoning, no unsupported exam subweights.

title: REE Mathematics — Matrices and Determinants
summary: Matrix dimensions and operations, determinants, invertibility and small linear systems with solution checks.

notes.heading: Core ideas
notes.body: Matrix dimensions determine which operations are defined. Addition requires equal dimensions; multiplication requires matching inner dimensions. A square matrix is invertible only when its determinant is nonzero. For a small system Ax=b, a solution may be found by elimination, determinant methods or an inverse when defined.

notes.heading: Worked check
notes.body: For 2x+y=11 and x−y=1, the coefficient matrix is [[2,1],[1,−1]] with determinant −3. Elimination gives x=4 and y=3; substitute both values into the original equations to verify.

notes.heading: Common errors and application
notes.body: Check row/column orientation before multiplication; do not divide by a zero determinant; preserve signs during row operations. Engineering-current labels may motivate a system, but the result must be checked against the original equations and units.

registered-electrical-engineering.rationale: PRC-listed matrices and determinants; engineering systems are contextual only.

title: REE Mathematics — Sequences and Series
summary: Arithmetic/geometric sequences, finite sums, recursive patterns, convergence language and engineering-model interpretation.

notes.heading: Core ideas
notes.body: An arithmetic sequence changes by a constant difference; a geometric sequence changes by a constant ratio. For a geometric sequence with first term a and ratio r, term n is a r^(n−1); a finite sum is a(1−r^n)/(1−r) when r≠1. State whether a question asks for a term or a sum.

notes.heading: Worked check
notes.body: If a=12 and r=0.9, the third term is 12(0.9)^2=9.72. The first-three-term sum is 12+10.8+9.72=32.52. These are different requested quantities.

notes.heading: Common errors and application
notes.body: Common mistakes are using exponent n instead of n−1, treating a difference as a ratio, and using an infinite-sum formula for a finite sequence. Explain what each term represents before calculating.

registered-electrical-engineering.rationale: PRC-listed sequences and series; use finite undergraduate examples.

title: REE Mathematics — Fourier Series and Laplace Transforms
summary: Periodic-function representation, Fourier coefficients at introductory level, Laplace transform rules and solving simple initial-value problems.

notes.heading: Core ideas
notes.body: Fourier series express a periodic function as a sum of a constant term and sinusoidal harmonics; coefficients depend on the stated period and interval. A Laplace transform maps a time-domain function into an algebraic function of s and incorporates initial conditions when transforming derivatives.

notes.heading: Worked check
notes.body: For f(t)=cos(3t), the one-sided Laplace transform is s/(s²+9) for Re(s)>0. The denominator uses angular frequency 3 rad/s; do not replace it with a frequency in hertz without conversion.

notes.heading: Common errors and application
notes.body: Check period/interval, coefficient normalization, transform table signs, initial-value terms and inverse-transform form. Use superposition for linear systems; do not present a transform result as a current engineering standard or a code requirement.

title: REE Allied — General Chemistry for Engineers

notes.heading: Worked check
notes.body: A solution contains 0.20 mol solute in 0.50 L solution. Molarity is n/V=0.40 mol/L. Keep volume in litres and distinguish the solution volume from solvent volume.

notes.heading: Common errors and application

notes.heading: Worked interpretation

title: REE Allied — Computer Fundamentals and Programming

notes.heading: Core ideas

Functions isolate a reusable operation; arrays/collections store ordered values. A program’s output is only as sound as the input validation and model assumptions.

notes.heading: Worked check
notes.body: For an engineering illustration, read V and R, require R>0, then compute I=V/R. With V=24 V and R=8 Ω, I=3 A. A robust routine rejects zero/negative resistance and labels the output unit; it does not silently accept invalid input.

notes.heading: Common errors and application

notes.heading: Common errors and application

title: Pressure-containing components: introductory thin-wall mechanics

title: Mechanical Engineering Law and licensure scope — R.A. 8495

notes.heading: Board and examination authority

notes.heading: Registration and practice
notes.body: Study only statutory categories, licensing boundaries, and Board powers expressly supported by R.A. 8495 and the currently PRC-linked implementing rules. Do not treat an old repealed-law provision as current merely because it appears in an older ethics document.

notes.heading: Ethics/code version firewall

title: Mechanical shop safety and current Philippine OSH boundaries
summary: Original, source-traceable study support for stable shop hazard-control principles and the current high-level duties and worker protections under R.A. 11058 and D.O. 252-25.

notes.heading: Stable hazard-control principles
notes.body: Identify the hazard, use the applicable guard or safeguard, isolate hazardous energy, address stored or residual energy, and verify a safe state before access. These are general decision principles; a scenario must supply any equipment-specific procedure.

notes.heading: Current Philippine OSH framework
notes.body: R.A. 11058 establishes general workplace OSH duties and worker protections. DOLE D.O. 252-25 is the revised IRR effective 2025-05-16 and replaces the prior D.O. 198-18 IRR. Use current controlling text for legal requirements; do not copy prior-order thresholds.

notes.heading: Bounded question scope
notes.body: Supported study topics include hazard recognition, safeguards, energy-isolation reasoning, worker information/reporting/refusal protections at the general statutory level, and safe maintenance decisions. title: Educational Foundations: Purpose, Institutions, and Social Effects
summary: Use educational-philosophy and sociology lenses to compare a stated purpose of schooling with classroom or policy effects. PRC scope remains the broad Professional Education area; the perspectives below are instructional tools, not separate blueprint leaves or item predictions.
notes: Learning objectives
Distinguish an intended educational function from an unintended consequence; compare perspectives on schooling; and support a claim about who benefits or faces a barrier with evidence from the case.
Purpose and cognitive demand

Recall can be useful evidence, but a learning goal may also require explanation, application, judgment, or evaluation. Match the assessment to the intended outcome instead of treating recall as the only purpose of education.
Education as a social institution

A functionalist lens asks what intended and unintended functions a school serves. A conflict or feminist lens asks how access and opportunities may be distributed unequally. An interactionist lens examines how everyday classroom interactions and labels shape experience. These are alternative analytical perspectives, not findings that every school has the same effect.
Analyze a policy case

State the policy’s intended purpose, identify which groups experience the result, separate observation from explanation, and ask what additional evidence would distinguish among plausible interpretations.
Philippine context and source limit

OpenStax examples are largely US-contextual and support general sociological concepts only. Apply Philippine law, policy, and local evidence before making a Philippine-specific claim.
